summary: Map stores key/value pairs and iterates in first-insertion order.
documentation: Map stores key/value pairs and iterates in first-insertion order. Updating a key changes its value without moving its position. Unlike ordinary object property lookup, keys do not collide with inherited method names.
inputs: Keys and values of any supported JavaScript types.
returns: set returns the Map; get returns its value or undefined when absent.
caution: Map is not directly represented by JSON.stringify as entries. Convert the final entries to an array for a JSON result.
scenarios: Accumulate sales by category while preserving arrival order.
Index product details without accidental prototype-property collisions.
Build an ordered lookup for imported status labels.
title: Total categories in arrival order
problem: Input is an array of [categoryString, integerCents] pairs. Return [categoryString, summedCents] pairs in first-seen category order. Include categories with a zero total and accept negative adjustments. Names such as __proto__ are ordinary categories.
goal: Use Map.get() and Map.set() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use a Map, add to each existing total, then return its entries as an array.
